think_procedure: To determine if jit_above_cost is a special knob, I need to analyze its behavior and possible values. The jit_above_cost parameter in PostgreSQL controls when Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation is triggered based on query cost. Let me examine its possible values: 1) It accepts numerical values representing cost thresholds (e.g., 100000, 500000) where JIT compilation will be enabled for queries exceeding this cost. 2) It has a special value of -1 which completely disables JIT compilation regardless of query cost. 3) When set to -1, it performs a fundamentally different function (disabling JIT) compared to its regular operation (enabling JIT above a cost threshold). This breaks the natural numerical order where higher values would normally mean higher thresholds.
